 10/24 Preview – No Morning Skate in NJ + In-Game Changes, Depth Scoring, Byfield’s Status Unknown, Devils Trade
 By Zach Dooley 
 4 hours ago 
 95 Comments 
 Share This Article 
 Share This Article 
 WHO: Los Angeles Kings (2-4-2) @ New Jersey Devils (5-3-0)
 WHAT: 2026-27 NHL Regular Season, Game 9/84
 WHEN: Saturday, October 24 @ 12:30 PM Pacific
 WHERE: Prudential Center – Newark, NJ
HOW TO FOLLOW: VIDEO: ABTV, DAZN – VIDEO: 830 AM KLAA, ESPN LA App, LA Kings App – TWITTER: @dooleylak & @lakings 
 TODAY’S MATCHUP: We’ve reached the hump day of the five-game roadtrip, as the LA Kings visit the New Jersey Devils for a Saturday-afternoon matinee in Newark.
 HEAD-TO-HEAD: Kings forward Artemi Panarin collected three points (1-2-3) in his only game played against the Devils as a member of the Kings, a 6-4 defeat in Newark back in March. Panarin has 48 points (16-32-48) in 38 career games played against New Jersey, his highest assist total against any opponent in the NHL. 
 KINGS VITALS: Considering the afternoon puck drop, the Kings did not hold a morning skate before today’s game against the Devils. 
 As such, unclear on who might get the start today. Should the Kings got back to Darcy Kuemper after a pair of strong performances, he is just 1-6-4 lifetime against the Devils, but with a .917 save percentage and a 2.49 goals-against average. Should the Kings turn to Anton Forsberg, he’s 3-4-1 in his career versus New Jersey, with a .899 save percentage and a 3.39 goals-against average. 
 For reference, here is last game’s Kings lineup, with the way they started the evening, before a couple of in-game swaps –
 Panarin – Laferriere – Kempe
Moore – Haula – Zuccarello
Lee – Laughton – Armia
Wright – Helenius – Perry 
 Gustafsson – Clarke
Edmundson – Doughty
Anderson – Dumoulin
 Kuemper
Forsberg
 The biggest question mark is the availability of forward Quinton Byfield, who is day-to-day with an upper-body injury. Byfield left Tuesday’s win over Washington in the first period and missed Thursday’s game against the Islanders. He would likely slot in as the 2C if healthy, with the lines adjusting around him. More below with a couple of thoughts. 
 UPDATE – No Byfield tonight. Expecting the same 18 skaters as the Islanders win. 
 DEVILS VITALS: Similar to the first two games on the trip, the Kings are facing an opponent today that is off to a strong start to the season, with New Jersey at 6-4-0 in the early goings. 
 Per Amanda Stein of NewJerseyDevils.com, here’s how the hosts lined up last time out in a win over Anaheim – 
 No changes for #NJDevils as they head into their matchup against the Ducks tonight. Lombardi and Dillon are out. Nico Daws took the first line rep, so I imagine he’s starting. We’ll see if he’s first off. https://t.co/prHNZCmPou
 — Amanda Stein (@amandacstein) October 22, 2026 
 Naturally, there will be some changes, as forward Dawson Mercer and goaltender Nico Daws are no longer on the team, following yesterday’s blockbuster trade with Winnipeg. Would expect that goaltender Jake Allen would get the start tonight, considering. Allen brings a lifetime record of 7-8-1 against the Kings into today’s matchup, with a .922 save percentage and a 2.43 goals-against average. 
 Storyline Of The Day – Lineup Thoughts All Around 
The Kings made some adjustments at the second intermission on Thursday.
 They led the game 2-1, but that was simply due to Artemi Panarin’s offensive brilliance and Darcy Kuemper’s heroics in net. The game flow was slanted almost entirely towards the Islanders, as the Kings weathered what felt like 40 straight minutes of a storm. 
 One of those adjustments was with the defensive pairings. Here’s Drew Doughty’s splits from that game.
 With Joel Edmundson, that pair was on the ice for five shot attempts for, 23 against. Then, the staff shuffled the pairs, moving Doughty alongside Erik Gustafsson. In 7:12 together, they were on the ice for nine attempts for compared to just two against. Edmundson then moved back with Brandt Clarke and they were just under even, while Mikey Anderson and Brian Dumoulin remained together. 
 I’ll be interested to see how the Kings line up today. I’d still like to see the Anderson/Clarke pair given some runway. We saw glimpses in the preseason but it’s never really been a thing when the points count. I can see why Gustafsson/Doughty could work too. With how things have gone, I don’t mind that Top-4, though I don’t think we’d see that drastic of a shift coming off a day off, without a morning skate. At the same time, Anderson and Dumoulin have been the team’s best pair on this trip. 
 Might’ve just been an in-game switch to try and quell New York’s momentum in the moment. It worked. Could see a revert back to how the Kings started the game, an alignment that’s led to back-to-back wins on the road. Or, maybe we see them start how it ended, with minor changes in play. 
 Up front, the question marks begin with Quinton Byfield, who I’d consider questionable for today. Whether he plays or not, the Kings have to find a way to get more goals beyond their first line. Right now, it feels like a threatening top line and a bottom nine that is passing the time.
 Regardless of who is in there, I wouldn’t be opposed to any sort of shuffle with those players. So far on this trip, the top line has been enough. That has a shelf life, though, and those guys can’t be asked to be on the scoresheet three times every single night. It’s happened twice in a row and it’s resulted in a pair of wins, which is good, but starting with the second line, the Kings need a lot more offensively than they’ve gotten to this point. 
 So, the lineup listed above it last game’s. Expecting to hear from Peter Laviolette at the rink this afternoon and I’ll enquire about an update on Byfield’s status. While his production has been among those who have been disappointing, with just two points in seven games played, he has averaged 22 goals and 53 points over the last three seasons, with most of his damage at even strength. If he plays, I’d expect to see him between Moore and Zuccarello, because that line never really got a chance with the injury and there is some potential there. It probably starts there and then you look for the trickle-down effect lower in the lineup, with several players capable of more than they’ve given. 
 3 To Watch For – 
– The biggest name in the transition, I think, was Gustafsson.
 Here’s a stat I think is pretty interesting. At even strength, Gustafsson is inside the NHL’s Top-10 in terms of the highest percentage of time spent in the offensive zone among defensemen. When he is on the ice, the Kings are playing offense. The Kings were outshot and outchanced against the Islanders but with Gustafsson on the ice, they held a 26-17 advantage in shot attempts. He was the only defenseman on the positive side of the ledger. 
 “Gus is one hell of a player,” forward Adrian Kempe said of his fellow countryman. “Offensively, he can make a lot of plays. Really fun player to play with, he’s got really high talent.”
 Artemi Panarin said that Gustafsson is “almost another forward” on the ice, which I think is something that high-end players like. When they find Gustafsson, they feel confident they’re going to get it back with possession and with his skating, he can activate at times, while also being able to recover. We all know the book on Gustafsson and that comes with defensive deficiencies. However, against the Islanders, Gustafsson led all Kings skaters in loose-puck recoveries and was tied for the team lead in defensive touches, per SportLOGIQ. 
 Had a good night and brings a different element to the group overall. Hope to see that continue. 
 – To add onto it, here’s a stat provided through ABTV – the last nine goals scored by Kings forwards against a goaltender – meaning excluding the empty-net goal in Washington – have come from Panarin, Laferriere or Kempe. 
 5-on-5 this season, the Kings have one goal from a forward who is not those players. It was Erik Haula’s deflection goal in San Jose, back in game two of the regular season. They have more 5-on-5 goals from their defensemen than they do from that group of forwards. 2-1. 
 Hard to recall it ever feeling like that large of a gulf. 
 The star players are performing. Artemi Panarin has scored a goal in every single road game this season. Adrian Kempe buried twice in Washington and has points in three straight. With Alex Laferriere now on that line, they’ve gelled very well and are carrying the way offensively.
 While it’s unclear whether or not Byfield will play today, it doesn’t matter. The Kings need more goals from their forwards, beyond the top line. If he’s in, that clearly starts with his line. If not, you look at players like Mats Zuccarello and Trevor Moore, even without Byfield, as guys who have to lead the way with secondary scoring. Both have produced in the past and haven’t gotten it going yet this season. The fourth line had probably their strongest night of the season against the Islanders, but the Kings haven’t gotten a goal there at any strength yet this season. The third line has had a ton of moving parts, but outside of the empty-net goal there hasn’t been much there either. 
 New Jersey is fairly deep. They have 11 players with four-point points and 15 players at three-plus points. The Kings have five each. Again, a storyline to watch in that area. 
 – Lastly, how about that trade.
 I know there were rumors that linked Connor Hellebuyck to the Kings, even though I don’t think there was much in it beyond a General Manager doing his due diligence. In looking at the return, I think that becomes pretty clear. For the Kings, they probably benefit from this trade, in that Dawson Mercer, a three-time 20-goal scorer, is removed from the lineup and Hellebuyck won’t play today.
 New Jersey has been a good defensive team, as the numbers show, without the saves to match in the early goings. Hellebuyck gives them an elite goaltender. He just won’t be that this afternoon, so that’s a plus. 
 Kings and Devils, Game 3 of 5 here on the trip. Game 3’s have gone well in the past for the Kings against New Jersey. Crazy to say it, but Los Angeles could lock in a winning trip with a win today, with two games to spare, even though ambitions should be higher than just that. See how things shake out in a building that has seemed to prove difficult over the years.
